drafts.title: Seeking Local TTS Options for Natural American English Dialogues with Gender Voice Switching
drafts.body:
I'm looking for local or free text-to-speech tools that can generate short dialogues in natural American English. The key requirement is the ability to switch between male and female voices within a conversation, ideally allowing combinations like male/male, male/female, and female/female. 

Coqui TTS (XTTS v2) was tried by another user but reportedly produced poor-quality output, which doesn’t meet the need for clear, natural-sounding dialogue. Given this, are there any other local TTS systems or open-source projects known to handle multi-speaker conversations with distinct gender voices effectively?

Since the source is from mid-2025 and the hardware details aren't specified, I’m curious if anyone has experience with recent or alternative local TTS tools that could better support this use case?

drafts.title: Local TTS for Two-Speaker Dialogues: Alternatives to Coqui XTTS v2 for Gender Voice Flexibility?
drafts.body:
A user reported needing a local TTS system to create short dialogues between two speakers, with flexibility to switch gender voices (male/male, male/female, female/female). Their experience with Coqui TTS (XTTS v2) suggested the output quality was lacking for this purpose as of June 2025.

This raises the question: are there other free or local TTS tools that handle multiple speakers with distinct gender voices more naturally? The ability to produce conversational exchanges with convincing voice differentiation seems key.

If anyone has encountered better options or workarounds for multi-voice local TTS setups, especially for American English, what tools or approaches have you found effective?
